cards.explanation: The LORD tells Moses and Eleazar the priest to take a census of Israel. He says, "Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers…" (Numbers 26:2). A census is a count, and this one is organized by the houses of their fathers. I think whoever had to keep track of all those names had a long day coming. Me? I'd lose count at the second tribe and start over.

The word is army, friends. The LORD says to count those "…twenty years of age or older who can serve in the army of Israel." (Numbers 26:2). So the count has an age line and a job line. It's not a list of everybody.

The number of names counted decides how big each tribe's share is, friends. The LORD says, "Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one; each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered." (Numbers 26:54). So the count wasn't just for show. The numbers decided how big the share would be.
The word is lot. The LORD says, "Indeed, the land must be divided by lot…" (Numbers 26:55). A lot is a way of choosing, a bit like drawing straws. Nobody gets to say "I want the spot by the river."

The answer is True, friends, and here's the reason the text gives. The Levites "were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites." (Numbers 26:62). They got their own count: 23,000, every male a month old or more. Same census, separate list.

The answer is False, bakers. "Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai." (Numbers 26:64). Not most, but not one. Whoa, that's a whole new crowd.

The word is die, friends. "For the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness." (Numbers 26:65). It's a heavy line, and the text says it plainly. That's why nobody from the Sinai count shows up in this new one, except two. Those two are Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
The two are Caleb and Joshua, friends. "Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 26:65). Two names out of a whole crowd. That's quite a short list of survivors.
